cards.text: One day Jesus is driving out a demon that was mute. The demon leaves, and the man who couldn't say a word starts talking. Friend, I went quiet for YEARS in a junk drawer, and now look at me: I can't STOP.

cards.question: The man who couldn't talk is talking now. How do the crowds react?

cards.text: But hold on. Not everybody's clapping, because some of them have their own theory about how Jesus does it.

cards.question: Some in the crowd say it is by ___, the prince of the demons, that Jesus drives out demons.
Others in the crowd test Jesus a different way. What do they demand from Him?

cards.text: Jesus knows their thoughts, and He tells them every kingdom divided against itself will be laid waste. And a house divided against a house will fall.

cards.question: Jesus says that if Satan is divided against himself, his kingdom will stand strong.

cards.text: Then Jesus hands their own claim right back to them. If He drives out demons by Beelzebul, by whom do their own sons drive them out?

cards.question: Jesus asks the accusers by whom their own sons drive out demons. What does He say those sons will be to them?

cards.text: Now Jesus turns it all the way around. What if He drives out demons by the finger of God?

cards.question: If Jesus drives out demons by the finger of God, then the ___ of God has come upon them.

cards.text: Then Jesus paints a picture: when a strong man, fully armed, guards his house, his possessions are secure. FULLY armed, friend, and the only armor I've ever had is an apron.

cards.question: A strong man guards his house fully armed. What happens when someone stronger attacks and overpowers him?

answers.text: The stronger one takes his armor and his plunder
The stronger one shares the house with him
The stronger one gives up and leaves him alone

cards.question: Jesus says whoever is not with Him is against Him, and whoever does not gather with Him scatters.

cards.text: Then Jesus tells what happens when an unclean spirit comes out of a man. It passes through arid places seeking rest, and it doesn't find it.

cards.question: With no rest to be found, the unclean spirit says it will return to the ___ it left.

cards.text: On its return, it finds the house swept clean and put in order. Swept AND organized, friend, which is more than anybody ever did for that junk drawer I lived in.

cards.question: The unclean spirit finds the house swept clean and put in order. What does it do next?

answers.text: Brings seven spirits more wicked than itself
Brings two spirits weaker than itself
Leaves the house and never comes back

cards.question: By the end, the man the unclean spirit left and came back to is better off than he was at first.

cards.text: As Jesus is still answering the people who said He drives out demons by Beelzebul, a woman in the crowd raises her voice: “Blessed is the womb that bore You, and blessed are the breasts that nursed You!” Speaking up right in the middle of the teaching is BOLD.

cards.question: A woman calls a blessing on the mother who bore and nursed Jesus. Who does Jesus say are blessed rather?

answers.text: Those who hear the word of God and obey it
Those who pray and fast in the temple daily
Those who give to the poor and tell no one

cards.text: The crowds keep growing, and remember those folks demanding a sign from heaven? Jesus calls this a wicked generation that demands a sign.

cards.question: Jesus says no sign will be given this generation except the sign of ___.
Jesus says that as the prophet Jonah was a sign to the Ninevites, the Son of Man will be a sign to this generation.

cards.text: Then Jesus brings up the Queen of the South, the queen of Sheba, who came from the ends of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, king of Israel (1 Kings 10:1). The ENDS of the earth, friend, and I won't even walk across my bakery when the timer goes off.

cards.question: The Queen of the South came to hear Solomon's wisdom, and Jesus says now One ___ than Solomon is here.
Jesus says the Queen of the South will rise at the judgment and defend the men of this generation.

cards.text: Then Jesus says the men of Nineveh will stand at the judgment with this generation and condemn it too.

cards.question: Why will the men of Nineveh condemn this generation at the judgment?

answers.text: They repented at the preaching of Jonah
They tore down the idols in their city
They built an altar to the God of Israel

cards.text: And just like with Solomon, Jesus says now One greater than Jonah is here.
Then Jesus switches pictures. No one lights a lamp and puts it in a cellar or under a basket, and that's like baking a perfect batch and hiding the box in the junk drawer.

cards.question: No one lights a lamp and hides it in a cellar. Where does it go instead so those who enter can see the light?

cards.text: Then Jesus brings the lamp picture closer to home. He says your eye is the lamp of your body.

cards.question: Jesus says that when your eyes are good, your whole body is full of darkness.
Jesus says the eye is the lamp of the body. What does He tell them to be careful about?

answers.text: That the light within them is not darkness
That their lamps never run out of oil
That no one walks off with their lamp

cards.text: Jesus finishes the lamp picture with a whole body full of light, with no part of it in darkness.

cards.question: If your whole body is full of light with no part of it in darkness, what does Jesus say you will be?

answers.text: Radiant as though a lamp were shining on you
Hidden as though you were down in a cellar
Weary as though you had walked all night

findings.problem: The question says someone stronger 'attacks and overpowers him,' which rules out the wrong answer 'The stronger one gives up and leaves him alone' and makes 'shares the house with him' hard to believe. Only one answer is left that a baker could take seriously.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The right answer says the stronger one 'takes his armor and his plunder.' Luke 11:22 says he takes away the armor in which the man trusted, and then he divides up his plunder. The answer turns 'divides up' into 'takes.'

rule.text: Call things what the text calls them.

findings.problem: This true or false card on Luke 11:23 follows a choice card with no story card before it. Nothing in the earlier cards sets up the 'with Me / against Me, gather / scatter' saying, so the baker has nothing to reason from and can only guess.

rule.text: Before each choice card, Papa Dorin's story card gives enough context that the baker can reason their way to the answer.

findings.problem: Card 15 says the spirit is already passing through arid places. That rules out the wrong answer 'desert' for the place it left, since it can't return to a desert it is still in.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: Card 12's setup and the question's own words ('hides it in a cellar,' 'so those who enter can see the light') rule out both wrong answers, 'Down under a bed' and 'Inside a clay jar,' because they are also hiding places. The 'Up' versus 'Down' wording also makes the right answer stand out.

rule.text: A setup line can't rule out the wrong answers either.

findings.problem: The question sets up a body 'full of light with no part of it in darkness,' which rules out 'Hidden as though you were down in a cellar' and 'Weary as though you had walked all night.' The right answer is the only one that matches the light picture, so it stands out.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.

findings.problem: Most story cards are plain narration with no reaction, comparison or disbelief from Papa Dorin: stop 1 cards 3, 6, 8, 10 and 15, and stop 2 cards 3, 9, 11, 14 and 17. Stop 2 card 1 ('is BOLD') is a mild reaction, not a laugh. The walkthrough reads more like a nice dad being pleasant than like a laugh-out-loud storyteller.

rule.text: When a moment can hold a real laugh without muddying a fact, he goes for it. If a line reads like a nice dad being pleasant, push it further.
